outcome.answer: Use a dynamic mixed-precision scheme that assigns different bit-widths to experts at runtime based on expert importance and sensitivity. DyMoE does this with importance-aware prioritization, depth-adaptive scheduling, and look-ahead prefetching to cut latency on edge hardware, while GEMQ uses global expert-level allocation plus router fine-tuning to reduce memory and accelerate inference [2, 5]. For a more runtime-focused approach, DPA-MoE makes routed experts any-precision by encoding weights into prefix-decodable chunks and allocating them using live router scores [7]. These papers target MoE inference on constrained devices, but they differ in whether they emphasize edge scheduling, global bit allocation, or post-routing precision control [2, 5, 7].
